scope.procedure: Read the MSA excerpt and the order form; challenge the claim that implementation services are distinct from the hosted SaaS subscription (ASC 606-10-25-19 through 25-21).

findings.summary: MSA Section 3.2 includes data migration in the implementation services, but the excerpt does not state whether Customer can use the hosted service before migration completes. If go-live depends on migration, the customer may not benefit from the subscription on its own, which weighs against distinctness. The basis recorded in j_impl_distinct does not address this dependency.

The examined MSA is an excerpt covering only Sections 3 and 9. Clauses elsewhere in the full agreement (e.g. customization or integration commitments) could contradict Section 3.1's statement that the hosted service is not materially modified; they were not available to this procedure.

limitations: Only the two scoped evidence files were examined; the price book and the full Master Subscription Agreement were out of scope.
Whether implementation services are distinct is a professional judgment; this procedure surfaces contrary indicators, it does not settle the question.

dispositions.note: Routed into the open j_impl_distinct judgment review; the go-live dependency point will be addressed in the judgment basis.
Full agreement reviewed in the demo contract system; no customization or integration commitments beyond Section 3.

notes: Synthetic demo attestation. The challenger model intentionally differs from the preparer model recorded in provenance/provenance.json.
